stem: Which of the following equations, together with \(4x - 6y = 10\), forms a system of linear equations that has infinitely many solutions?
solution: A system has infinitely many solutions when both equations describe the same line, that is, when one is a constant multiple of the other.
The other choices either change the sign of the constant (parallel line, no solution) or change the slope (one solution).

explanation.A: Incorrect. The left side is \(-\frac{3}{2}\) times \(4x - 6y\), but \(-\frac{3}{2}(10) = -15\), not \(15\); this line is parallel to the given one, so there is no solution.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This line has slope \(-\frac{2}{3}\), while \(4x - 6y = 10\) has slope \(\frac{2}{3}\); the lines cross in exactly one point.
explanation.C: Correct. This is \(-\frac{3}{2}\) times \(4x - 6y = 10\), so it describes the same line.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Halving \(4x - 6y = 10\) gives \(2x - 3y = 5\), not \(-5\); this line is parallel to the given one, so there is no solution.

verify:
x, y = symbols('x y')
L = value(choices[answer].split('=')[0]) - value(choices[answer].split('=')[1])
inf = [k for k in choices if len(linsolve([4*x - 6*y - 10, value(choices[k].split('=')[0]) - value(choices[k].split('=')[1])], [x, y]).free_symbols) > 0]
assert inf == [answer]
assert simplify(L - Rational(-3, 2)*(4*x - 6*y - 10)) == 0
